speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) at the recent ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting on 18 January 2019, what did ASEAN agree to do in addressing the challenges of repatriation of Rohingya refugees, namely, lack of security, citizenship status and access to education and employment; and (b) given the current ground situation in Rakhine, how will ASEAN be working with the Bangladeshi government to ensure that the refugees have access to education and employment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As usual, the subject of the Rakhine State came up for extensive informal discussion amongst the Foreign Ministers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We focused on efforts by ASEAN to support the refugees as well as Myanmar and, in particular, focused on the safe and voluntary repatriation of these refugees.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The needs assessment team will help us identify the possible areas of cooperation for ASEAN to lend its support.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think, just as importantly, the presence of an ASEAN needs assessment team will also help enhance the confidence and trust of the refugees on the ground, and we were hoping that it would help create a conducive environment for the sustainable and voluntary repatriation, resettlement and, ultimately, rebuilding of lives on the part of the refugees.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, I am sorry to note that in light of the recent outbreak of violence, which this time involves the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army – this is a different community from the Muslim refugees, so, the point is, you now have a triangular situation of violence amongst the stakeholders in Rakhine State.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I would emphasise it is just as important that the manner of the repatriation be voluntary, safe, dignified and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have met the Prime Minister of Bangladesh and also the State Counsellor of Myanmar just two months ago and I am absolutely certain that the leadership of both countries is committed to the ultimate repatriation of the refugees and, in fact, the two countries have had extensive discussions on how to bring this about.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The reason for this is that you need sufficient confidence on the part of the refugees before you can begin repatriation in a voluntary, safe and dignified way.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We cannot do so on behalf of Myanmar and, ultimately, Myanmar has to sort out its own political challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: During my visits to the refugee camp at the end of November last year, I had the opportunity to speak to some of the refugees.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One, security – safety for their families; and two, livelihood, what would they do to make a living when they go back?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These are essentials that need to be sorted out before the refugees would be willing to go back.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: More fundamentally, Myanmar has to address the root causes of the problem.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And it is worth emphasising that this has been a long-standing, chronic problem for many decades, if not a century or more.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The late Mr Kofi Annan and the Advisory Commission on the Rakhine State had provided comprehensive recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Furthermore, the Myanmar government established an Independent Commission of Enquiry, and this, if properly pursued, would provide for accountability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope that this Commission will be able to carry out its investigations with full impartiality.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN countries, including Singapore, have provided assistance to Myanmar on a bilateral basis.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But ultimately, I need to emphasise that it is the responsibility of the Myanmar government and all the other stakeholders to reach a viable and durable political solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And on matters like these, Mr Speaker, we cannot expect any quick fixes.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I was also there in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, in my personal capacity with one of my community projects, Playground of Joy, last December.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And I totally agree with the Minister that the two main concerns that he brought up – security for their family and livelihood – did come up as well.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I would also like to add that a third concern was education that was mentioned to me.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And so, I have two questions for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One would be, has ASEAN, and Singapore as well, come to any sort of contingency plan should the funding by United Nations (UN) and the different donors for Cox's Bazar and also the different refugee camps around Asia and ASEAN run out, what would we do?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that we cannot impose a hard date on when the repatriation could happen.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I would love to know what we have in mind in terms of contingency plans for that.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Also, at the same time, can we do anything in the meantime, if not for the livelihood, for the education of the children in Bangladesh, the ones who are settling in Bangladesh at the moment?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If the Member had been there, I think the Member would join me in commending the incredible generosity and efforts that the Bangladesh government and people have made to welcome, protect and support these refugees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you have gone to the biggest camp there, for as far as the eye can see, to the horizon, you would have seen tents, habitations and homes that were built.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As a previous Environment Minister, the things I look out for: cooking, drains, wells, toilets, environment protection – all those measures have been put in place.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the first point is to commend Bangladesh and the international community, including the non-government organisations (NGOs) such as yours, that have supported and have actually done an incredible job.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And as I said, better prospects are not going to occur in a hurry.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the latest bout of violence, involving this time the Arakan community, complicates matters even further.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Do I foresee a sudden cessation of support from the UN, the UN agencies and the International NGOs for the refugees there?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: No, I do not foresee that contingency occurring, at least not for the foreseeable future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the meantime, I need to commend the work of NGOs, such as yours.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we will all try, we are trying – and I commend the Member for making a difference on the ground.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we also need to be realistic on timeframes and also on the ultimately limited role that we play.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And as I have said at the beginning, at every ASEAN meeting, this matter is discussed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It may not be on the formal agenda, but I can guarantee you that it takes up a significant amount of bandwidth on the part of both the Leaders at the Summit level as well as the Foreign Ministers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But if I could bring up a point I raised before, which is really the fourth request on the refugees, which, again, is about citizenship.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am not asking for the Singapore Government to give them citizenship in Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I am asking whether this issue can be discussed at a deeper level at the ASEAN meetings because that really is one of the roots of the problems.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It goes to the heart of sovereignty, it goes to the heart of the construction of how a country looks at itself and identify who is in and who is out.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would humbly put to the Member that because this is such a fundamental point, it has to be settled within the country, through the political system, processes and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: First of all, ASEAN is a group that works by consensus.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, is there division amongst ASEAN members on this matter?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Second, related to that, does division on this matter prevent us reaching agreement on other points which are more important?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And, if so, is this a matter that should rightly be because ASEAN Ministers spend a lot of time on it and if it sours relationships and prevents ASEAN moving on other matters where agreement can be reached?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would not say that there are divisions within ASEAN on this matter.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would say that there are different perspectives and different weights given by the different ASEAN countries, which often reflect our own domestic considerations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But again, I just want to come back to this point that no society, no community, can progress without first finding its way to creating their version of a fair and just society, without providing security, without providing education, jobs and livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, my one line to the Member is that there are no divisions within ASEAN.
